Check compatibility of traits.build object

Source: R/check_compatibility.R
check_compatibility.Rd

Function to check whether the data object has been compiled by the traits.build workflow and therefore has a data structure that is appropriate for use with traits.use functions.

A database built by traits.build 2.3 or later records the version of the traits.build data model its tables follow, in metadata$data_model_version (see get_data_model_version()). It is compatible if that version's major number is one this version of traits.use reads (supported_data_model_majors()). A database without that field is compatible if metadata$related_identifiers says it was compiled by traits.build, which is how releases built before the field existed, such as AusTraits 7.0.0 and earlier, are recognised.

A flat table (see database_format()) is accepted only when single_table_allowed is TRUE, and, if flatten_database() stamped it with a data model version, only if that version is supported; otherwise it stops with an error saying the function needs the relational database. Anything that is neither a relational database nor a traits table stops with an error.

Usage

check_compatibility(
  database,
  single_table_allowed = FALSE,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

Arguments

database

traits.build database (list object), or a flat table from one

single_table_allowed

logical: can the calling function take a flat table (a flattened database, or a traits table)? Defaults to FALSE

call

the calling function's environment, named in errors

Value

logical (T/F) output and messaging for incompatible versions
